properties.statement: THE THING dev_storyflow WOULD MOST LIKE CLOSED: NOTHING LINKS A CAPABILITY TO THE AUTHORING SURFACE THAT FEEDS IT, SO A CAPABILITY CAN BE `realized`, BUILT, RENDERING — AND DEAD. Reported 2026-08-08 by sb-boss ab2291fa, item 5, explicitly labelled 'the thing that would have saved the most time today' and 'the gap I would most like closed'. `cap:storybook_output` was status `realized`, its component was built, its proposer existed, its frontend rendered — AND THE CAPABILITY WAS DEAD, because no UI writes the field it consumes. EVERY EXISTING EDGE TYPE WAS SATISFIABLE WITHOUT THAT SURFACE EXISTING: REALIZES, SATISFIES, DEPENDS_ON and CONSUMES were all present and all honest. THE DIAGNOSTIC COST IS THE MEASURE OF IT: three people produced three different root causes, and all three were greppable mechanisms — because a greppable mechanism is the only kind of cause a search can find. The true cause, 'nobody ever writes this', HAD NO ARTIFACT TO FIND. THIS IS A VOCABULARY GAP, NOT A DETECTOR BUG: detect_gaps cannot ask about a surface the design has no way to say is required, which is req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots in its sharpest form to date — a detector that finds the missing half of something BEGUN, over a thing that was never begun and cannot be expressed. REFLOW2 HAS ALREADY MET THE INSTANCE AND NOT THE GENERAL CASE: req:the-store-is-reachable-from-a-session says 'a capability nothing can call is not delivered - the content store needs a surface', which is this same insight scoped to one capability and written by hand. Nothing generalises it and nothing detects it. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WORTH THINKING ABOUT: the missing edge is not another machine-to-machine dependency, it is the HUMAN INPUT PATH — where a person or an upstream system actually puts the data the capability consumes — and reflow2 models actors INTERACTS_WITH capabilities but never that an interaction is REQUIRED for the capability to function at all.
